checks.invariant: grep's result, including its truncation records, depends only on rows the caller's Visibility admits
checks.result: The candidate budget (grep.py:254-255, nominated_count from the unfiltered posting kernel) and the scan-tier overflow flag (scope.py:279-295, LIMIT limit+1 with no view predicate) are computed before the per-row view.holds check (grep.py:260-262, 301-305). The grep_rows docstring (grep.py:185-186) already says hidden candidates count against the budget. A bounded local run under the sandbox showed the truncation record appearing or not depending on hidden rows that a direct read reports as not_found.

checks.invariant: glean's BM25 statistics come from the visible set for a caller with partial rights
checks.result: _visible_lexicon (glean.py:709-776) recomputes N, avg_dl and per-term df over the chunks the view admits, so corpus-wide lex_df/lex_stats are not exposed to a partial caller. The overlay fetch (glean.py entries_for_scan with OVERLAY_BUDGET) has the same pre-view overflow shape as grep's scan side. I recorded it as a variant of the same root cause and did not investigate it further.

checks.invariant: read/stat/ls/tree/glob show a row only after Visibility.shows/reads, and hidden rows read exactly as absent
checks.result: _viewed (backend.py:1511-1557) resolves rights and refuses anonymous callers before any read, then passes a Visibility. In reads.py, _point_rows, _screen, _classify_unresolved, _children_by_parent, tree_rows (_visible_rows) and glob_rows each judge every fetched row in Python. Rows the caller can only list come back bare, and hidden ancestors go through seen_kinds, so a miss is classified the same way an absent row is. glob max_count truncates after filtering. Tombstones keep their label and owner, and the trash view (_trash_roots, the trashed road) applies the same view, so I found no extra visibility through /.vfs/trash. The RightsCache key (subject_names) cannot collide between anonymous and named callers, because the names are reserved (authority.py Principal.__post_init__). No candidate found in what I read.

unresolved: Review was cut short. Road derivation helpers _owned_beneath/_open_beneath (rights.py) and descent.classify_miss were not read in full, so equal answers for hidden and absent rows on every miss path are not fully established.

candidates.title: grep's candidate-budget and scan-overflow truncation records count rows the caller cannot see
candidates.description: For a caller with partial rights, grep (and, by the same shape, glean's overlay) computes whether a call hit its budget from candidate rows before the per-row Visibility check. Whether a truncation warning appears, and how many rows come back, can therefore change with the presence or content of rows the caller cannot read, even though a direct read of those rows reports not_found. This breaks the stated rule that hidden rows read exactly as absent, for derived search outputs.
candidates.claimed_root_cause: nominated_count (grep.py:254) comes from the posting kernel over all entries in the glob allow-list, and entries_for_scan (scope.py:279-295) sets overflow from an unfiltered LIMIT limit+1. Both happen before view.holds (grep.py:260-262, 301-305), so the truncation records and the remaining budget take hidden rows into account.

trace.description: grep runs under _viewed with a partial Visibility
index-side candidate ids and nominated_count come from the unfiltered posting kernel
scan-tier fetch with LIMIT limit+1 and no view predicate sets overflow
truncation records built from those hidden-inclusive counts are returned to the caller

evidence.description: Docstring says the candidate budget still counts hidden candidates
The view check runs only after the budget has been computed
Overflow is set from the unfiltered row count

blockers: My run was halted before I could write a promoted evidence artifact, so no local check is attached and the local observation needs independent reproduction.
The glean overlay variant (OVERLAY_BUDGET) was identified from source only and not run.

validation_plan.local: With InMemoryStorage under the sandbox, as a named caller with no rights under one prefix, compare grep's truncation records and row counts for calls whose scope includes that hidden prefix, with and without a hidden row present. If they differ, the finding is confirmed. Fix: compute budgets and overflow only after view.holds, or push the visibility predicate into the nomination and scan statements, and replace the 'counts hidden candidates' docstring note with a regression test showing grep output is identical whether or not hidden rows are present.

hardening: glean partial-caller BM25 statistics are computed over the visible set (glean.py _visible_lexicon), so the corpus-wide lex_df/lex_stats rows are not exposed to a partial caller; keep a parity test for this.
